title: The Macaron block
goal:
Section 2.4 (Equation 1) defines one Conformer block. Two feed-forward modules sandwich the attention and convolution modules, and each adds only half of its output:

$$
\tilde x = x + \tfrac12 \mathrm{FFN}(x), \quad x' = \tilde x + \mathrm{MHSA}(\tilde x), \quad x'' = x' + \mathrm{Conv}(x'), \quad y = \mathrm{LayerNorm}\!\left(x'' + \tfrac12 \mathrm{FFN}(x'')\right)
$$

Write `conformer_block(x, ffn1, mhsa, conv, ffn2, final_ln)`. `x` is a `(T, d)` array. The other five arguments are functions from a `(T, d)` array to a `(T, d)` array. `ffn1` is the first feed-forward module and `ffn2` is the second. Return `y`. Each module adds its own pre-norm inside the function you receive, so this function only wires the residual connections.
hints: Write one line per equation: `x1 = x + 0.5 * ffn1(x)`, then `x2 = x1 + mhsa(x1)`, and so on.
Each module reads the output of the previous line, not the original `x`.
The two feed-forward modules are different functions with their own weights. Call `ffn1` first and `ffn2` last.
Only the feed-forward residuals use the factor 0.5. The attention and convolution residuals add the full output.
Apply `final_ln` once, to the sum after the second feed-forward residual.
